parsedVerdict.reasoning: AdvanceOrderUseCase.execute does the work an application-layer use case is meant to do. It loads the aggregate through the OrderRepository port, hands the state transition to the domain (order.advanceTo(target)), calls the StockService when an order ships, saves the order through the port and maps the result to a DTO with toOrderDto. The file has no persistence code: it uses no SQL, ORM or storage APIs. It has no transport or framework code: it uses no HTTP, request/response objects or decorators. It also does not implement business rules itself, because the state-transition logic stays inside the domain entity. The check `if (target === "shipped") this.stock.dispatch(...)` is a borderline case. One could argue that a domain event belongs on the aggregate. However, coordinating between an aggregate and a separate domain service is a normal application-layer responsibility. Raising a not_found DomainError when the order is missing is also normal use-case behaviour. No ADR prose was provided that would contradict this.
